---
title: "Lesson 2: Setting up"
---

## 1. Install Quarto

1. Download the installer for your computer from [quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/).
2. Run it and accept the defaults.
3. Check it works. Open a terminal (Terminal on Mac, or the terminal inside your editor) and run:

```bash
quarto --version
```

You should see a version number, like `1.10.18`.

::: {.callout-note}
RStudio and Positron include a copy of Quarto, but installing it separately gives you the newest version and makes the `quarto` command available in any terminal.
:::

## 2. Install R and two packages

Pages that run R code need R plus the `rmarkdown` and `knitr` packages.

1. Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) if you don't have it.
2. In R, run:

```r
install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "knitr"))
```

For the chart examples in the exercises, also install `ggplot2`:

```r
install.packages("ggplot2")
```

## 3. Set up your editor

Pick the editor you use. The tabs on every page of this training remember your choice.

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## Positron

[Positron](https://positron.posit.co/) is Posit's newer editor. It has R, Python, and Quarto support built in.

1. Install Positron.
2. Open it and start an R session (the interpreter picker at the top right).
3. Nothing else to install: Quarto support is included.

**Command Palette:** most Quarto actions are in the Command Palette: **Cmd + Shift + P** (Mac) or **Ctrl + Shift + P** (Windows). Type `Quarto` to see them.

## VS Code

1. Install [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/).
2. Open the **Extensions** view (the four-squares icon in the left bar) and install:
   - **Quarto** (by Quarto)
   - **R** (by REditorSupport)
3. In R, install the language server, which the R extension uses:
   ```r
   install.packages("languageserver")
   ```

**Command Palette:** **Cmd + Shift + P** (Mac) or **Ctrl + Shift + P** (Windows). Type `Quarto` to see Quarto actions.

## RStudio

1. Install a recent [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) (2022.07 or later supports Quarto).
2. Nothing else to install: Quarto support is included.

**Where things are:** the **Render** button sits above an open `.qmd` file. Website projects also get a **Build** tab (top-right pane).

:::

## 4. Check everything

Run this in a terminal:

```bash
quarto check
```

It reports whether Quarto can find R and `knitr`. Look for ✓ (or `OK`) next to **R installation** and **knitr**. If R isn't found, restart your editor after installing R, and run `quarto check` again.

## Checklist

- [ ] `quarto --version` shows a version number
- [ ] R installed, with `rmarkdown`, `knitr`, and `ggplot2`
- [ ] Editor installed (and, for VS Code, the Quarto and R extensions)
- [ ] `quarto check` finds R and knitr
- [ ] [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/download/) (or Git) set up, from the [Git and GitHub training](../intro-to-github/02-setup.qmd)
